doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

chapter: Session stories and why he was hired
title: Acoustic guitar overdub on 'The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face'
summary: Bucky recognizes an overdub he played to accompany an already-recorded vocal, without knowing it would be a hit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Okay well when I came in I saw this music by Mario Tedesco —
Castelnuovo.
Castelnuovo. A nice Irish boy.
Newcastle.
Well it reminded me of this. See if you recognize this one.
[audio interlude “First Time Ever I Saw Your Face”]
Did you get it yet? That’s you on acoustic guitar?
Get out of here. What am I playing? Oh yeah.
That was kind of a different date.
Yeah. Well they asked me to do something without the music, and that’s what I did.
You mean you had no music?
Well we had just the chords but they wanted something. That’s what I worked up.
It was pretty good. Now do you recall coming home from — was that like a New York date?
Yeah. It was an overdub. She had already made the record.
Oh it was an overdub.
And she wanted something different.
Okay. Were you hearing her singing?
Yeah. And I played like I was accompanying her.
Oh. See, that’s the backstory. That’s very interesting. Did you come home and say, “I just played on a hit”?
No.
Have you ever known you were playing on a hit?
No.
Gee. That’s very interesting.
